page.layout: One printed page, single text column. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Text block with a centred heading (EXERC. XI.) and a subtitle in capitals and italic, then running text. No margin notes. Catchword/signature: "D 2" at foot (signature).

main_text.p: est ἐντελέχεια, & perfectio naturalis corporis. Igitur nulla anima à genitore in semé eius deriuat: hoc est, nullum semen actu animatum est, sed duntaxat potentia: eò quòd de materiæ potentia à proprij agentis ui ipsa forma in actum deducitur.
main_text.head: EXERC. XI.
QVATVOR MVNDI ELEMENTIS non solum rerum generabilium materiæ, sed etiam formæ sunt acceptæ referendæ.
main_text.p: Quemadmodum è uaria quatuor elementorum Mundi permistione, uariæ prodeunt secundæ ac indiuiduæ materiæ ad plurimas formarum differentias suscipiendas idoneæ: ita profectò ex ijsdem diuersis elementorum permistionibus diuersæ quoque emergunt essentiales formæ. Educuntur enim ui agentis proximi, humana dempta (cuius origo diuina est) è propriarum materiarum potentijs. Quòd sane haud quaquam fieri contingeret, nisi in ipsis elementis inessent potetia. Atque licet diuersis ex materijs in actus educantur: attamen tantus ille formarum proventus non minus subiectis rite præpara-tis,

page.notes: Greek word "ἐντελέχεια" as printed in the first line is partly illegible in the scan; reading "ἐντελέχεια" is likely but uncertain. Printed "potetia" and "proventus" are as printed. Heading "QVATVOR" begins with a large initial Q, transcribed as Q. Last line of the text continues on the next page ("tis," at the foot appears to be the catchword-like continuation of "præpara-tis," and is printed at the foot of the column after the signature; it is treated as the end of the paragraph). Printed "D 2" is the signature. Two marginal shadows at the top right are show-through or stains and are not transcribed.
